correctness.rationale: Substitution of zero mixing into the source's two exact transition-parameter formulas leaves an absolute value of alpha times beta minus four and hence precisely the claimed unordered pair, with the product-four locus only exchanging labels. The source's channel spectral theorem then yields each region and multiplicity by comparing the two parameters with one. In the subcritical rectangle, Theorem 7.2 gives a bounded difference from the sum of the two Jacobi counts, and the cited Jacobi asymptotic converts the two parameter gaps into the stated alpha- and beta-side inverse-square-root constants. The verifier's numerical factorization checks agree with this direct analytic specialization.

originality.rationale: Exner–Lipovský already give the exact two transition parameters for the full four-real-parameter contact interaction, the channel spectral trichotomy, the additive absolutely-continuous multiplicity statement, the bounded comparison of the discrete count with the two Jacobi channels, and the needed Jacobi asymptotic. Setting the mixing parameter to zero turns their square root into the absolute value of alpha times beta minus four and immediately yields the two decoupled channel parameters. Every part of the submitted rectangular phase diagram and bicritical asymptotic is therefore a direct specialization and algebraic restatement of the stronger published theorem.

value.rationale: The rectangular picture is a useful visualization of a natural slice, but all of its scientific content follows by direct substitution into the already-published general formulas and theorems, followed by first-order algebra. Under the required bar against parameter specialization and mechanically implied corollaries, it does not constitute an independently valuable result.

final_claim: On the positive zero-mixing slice of the Exner–Lipovský contact-interaction model, the two transition parameters decouple into sqrt(2)/alpha and beta/(2 sqrt(2)); the absolutely-continuous spectrum therefore has the stated rectangular two-threshold phase diagram and multiplicities, and the discrete-state count has the stated sum of two inverse-square-root divergences at the bicritical corner.
scientific_limitations: Rejected for decisive prior implication and routine parameter-specialization value, not for correctness.
